passages.text: This is the vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem that Isaiah son of Amoz saw during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was the son of Amoz.
Isaiah saw a vision.
This vision was about Judah and Jerusalem.
Isaiah saw this vision during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.
Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings of Judah.
passages.original: חֲזוֹן֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־ אָמ֔וֹץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה עַל־ יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם בִּימֵ֨י עֻזִּיָּ֧הוּ יוֹתָ֛ם אָחָ֥ז יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ מַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: Listen, O heavens, and give ear, O earth, for the LORD has spoken: “I have raised children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against Me.
passages.sermon:
Isaiah is a prophet.
Isaiah is the son of Amoz.
Isaiah saw a vision from God.
God spoke to Isaiah about Judah and Jerusalem.
God spoke during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
God calls the heavens to listen.
God calls the earth to pay attention.
The LORD has spoken.
God says, “I raised children.
I brought them up.
They rebelled against Me.”
passages.original: שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ וְהַאֲזִ֣ינִי אֶ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּ֑ר בָּנִים֙ גִּדַּ֣לְתִּי וְרוֹמַ֔מְתִּי וְהֵ֖ם פָּ֥שְׁעוּ בִֽי׃

passages.text: The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master’s manger, but Israel does not know; My people do not understand.”
passages.sermon:
Isaiah is a prophet.
Isaiah is the son of Amoz.
Isaiah speaks about Judah and Jerusalem.
God speaks through Isaiah.
An ox knows its owner.
A donkey knows its master’s manger.
Israel does not know God.
God’s people do not understand.
passages.original: יָדַ֥ע שׁוֹר֙ קֹנֵ֔הוּ וַחֲמ֖וֹר אֵב֣וּס בְּעָלָ֑יו יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔ע עַמִּ֖י לֹ֥א הִתְבּוֹנָֽן׃

passages.text: Alas, O sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a brood of evildoers, children of depravity! They have forsaken the LORD; they have despised the Holy One of Israel and turned their backs on Him.
passages.sermon:
Israel is a sinful nation.
The people carry much guilt.
They are a group of evildoers.
They are children who destroy.
They have left the LORD.
They have hated the Holy One of Israel.
They have turned away from Him.
passages.original: ה֣וֹי׀ גּ֣וֹי חֹטֵ֗א עַ֚ם כֶּ֣בֶד עָוֺ֔ן זֶ֣רַע מְרֵעִ֔ים בָּנִ֖ים מַשְׁחִיתִ֑ים עָזְב֣וּ אֶת־ יְהוָ֗ה נִֽאֲצ֛וּ אֶת־ קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נָזֹ֥רוּ אָחֽוֹר׃

passages.text: Why do you want more beatings? Why do you keep rebelling? Your head has a massive wound, and your whole heart is afflicted.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
Israel is a sinful nation.
Israel continues to rebel against God.
God asks Israel, “Why do you want more punishment?”
God asks, “Why do you keep turning away?”
Every head is sick.
Every heart is in pain.
passages.original: עַ֣ל מֶ֥ה תֻכּ֛וּ ע֖וֹד תּוֹסִ֣יפוּ סָרָ֑ה כָּל־ רֹ֣אשׁ לָחֳלִ֔י וְכָל־ לֵבָ֖ב דַּוָּֽי׃

passages.text: From the sole of your foot to the top of your head, there is no soundness— only wounds and welts and festering sores neither cleansed nor bandaged nor soothed with oil.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the sinful nation of Israel.
He describes the people as completely afflicted.
From the sole of your foot to the top of your head, you have no health.
You have only wounds.
You have bruises.
You have open sores.
No one has cleaned your wounds.
No one has bandaged you.
No one has soothed your sores with oil.
passages.original: מִכַּף־ רֶ֤גֶל וְעַד־ רֹאשׁ֙ אֵֽין־ בּ֣וֹ מְתֹ֔ם פֶּ֥צַע וְחַבּוּרָ֖ה וּמַכָּ֣ה טְרִיָּ֑ה לֹא־ זֹ֙רוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א חֻבָּ֔שׁוּ וְלֹ֥א רֻכְּכָ֖ה בַּשָּֽׁמֶן׃

passages.text: Your land is desolate; your cities are burned with fire. Foreigners devour your fields before you— a desolation demolished by strangers.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
Your land is empty and ruined.
Fire has destroyed your cities.
Foreigners eat your fields while you watch.
Strangers have made your land a wasteland.
Your land is destroyed like a place overthrown by outsiders.
passages.original: אַרְצְכֶ֣ם שְׁמָמָ֔ה עָרֵיכֶ֖ם שְׂרֻפ֣וֹת אֵ֑שׁ אַדְמַתְכֶ֗ם לְנֶגְדְּכֶם֙ זָרִים֙ אֹכְלִ֣ים אֹתָ֔הּ וּשְׁמָמָ֖ה כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֥ת זָרִֽים׃

passages.text: And the Daughter of Zion is abandoned like a shelter in a vineyard, like a shack in a cucumber field, like a city besieged.
passages.sermon:
The Daughter of Zion remains alone.
She is like a shelter left in a vineyard.
She is like a hut standing in a cucumber field.
She is like a city surrounded by enemies.
No one protects her.
She stands abandoned and exposed.
passages.original: וְנוֹתְרָ֥ה בַת־ צִיּ֖וֹן כְּסֻכָּ֣ה בְכָ֑רֶם כִּמְלוּנָ֥ה בְמִקְשָׁ֖ה כְּעִ֥יר נְצוּרָֽה׃

passages.text: Unless the LORD of Hosts had left us a few survivors, we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is God who commands armies.
God left us a few survivors.
If God had not left us survivors, we would have become like Sodom.
We would have resembled Gomorrah.
passages.original: לוּלֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הוֹתִ֥יר לָ֛נוּ שָׂרִ֖יד כִּמְעָ֑ט כִּסְדֹ֣ם הָיִ֔ינוּ לַעֲמֹרָ֖ה דָּמִֽינוּ׃ס

passages.text: Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom; listen to the instruction of our God, you people of Gomorrah!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
He calls them rulers of Sodom and people of Gomorrah.
God commands them to hear His word.
God tells them to listen to the instruction of our God.
passages.original: שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה קְצִינֵ֣י סְדֹ֑ם הַאֲזִ֛ינוּ תּוֹרַ֥ת אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ עַ֥ם עֲמֹרָֽה׃

passages.text: “What good to Me is your multitude of sacrifices?” says the LORD. “I am full from the burnt offerings of rams and the fat of well-fed cattle; I take no delight in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD asks about the value of many sacrifices.
The LORD says, “What good are your many sacrifices to Me?”
The LORD says, “I have had enough of burnt offerings from rams.”
The LORD says, “I have had enough of the fat from well-fed cattle.”
The LORD says, “I do not delight in the blood of bulls.”
The LORD says, “I do not delight in the blood of lambs.”
The LORD says, “I do not delight in the blood of goats.”
passages.original: לָמָּה־ לִּ֤י רֹב־ זִבְחֵיכֶם֙ יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שָׂבַ֛עְתִּי עֹל֥וֹת אֵילִ֖ים וְחֵ֣לֶב מְרִיאִ֑ים וְדַ֨ם פָּרִ֧ים וּכְבָשִׂ֛ים וְעַתּוּדִ֖ים לֹ֥א חָפָֽצְתִּי׃

passages.text: When you come to appear before Me, who has required this of you— this trampling of My courts?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Judah.
God calls them to appear before Him.
God asks them a question.
God says, “Who asked you to come before Me?”
God says, “Who required you to trample My courts?”
passages.original: כִּ֣י תָבֹ֔אוּ לֵרָא֖וֹת פָּנָ֑י מִי־ בִקֵּ֥שׁ זֹ֛את מִיֶּדְכֶ֖ם רְמֹ֥ס חֲצֵרָֽי׃

passages.text: Bring your worthless offerings no more; your incense is detestable to Me— your New Moons, Sabbaths, and convocations. I cannot endure iniquity in a solemn assembly.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to His people.
He commands them to stop bringing worthless offerings.
He says their incense disgusts Him.
He rejects their New Moon festivals.
He rejects their Sabbaths.
He rejects their sacred gatherings.
He cannot endure evil mixed with worship.
He refuses to accept sin in their assemblies.
passages.original: לֹ֣א תוֹסִ֗יפוּ הָבִיא֙ מִנְחַת־ שָׁ֔וְא קְטֹ֧רֶת תּוֹעֵבָ֛ה הִ֖יא לִ֑י חֹ֤דֶשׁ וְשַׁבָּת֙ קְרֹ֣א מִקְרָ֔א לֹא־ אוּכַ֥ל אָ֖וֶן וַעֲצָרָֽה׃

passages.text: I hate your New Moons and your appointed feasts. They have become a burden to Me; I am weary of bearing them.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God says, “I hate your New Moon festivals.
I hate your appointed feasts.
These celebrations are a burden to Me.
I am tired of carrying them.”
passages.original: חָדְשֵׁיכֶ֤ם וּמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם֙ שָׂנְאָ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֔י הָי֥וּ עָלַ֖י לָטֹ֑רַח נִלְאֵ֖יתִי נְשֹֽׂא׃

passages.text: When you spread out your hands in prayer, I will hide My eyes from you; even though you multiply your prayers, I will not listen. Your hands are covered with blood.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God sees their actions.
When you spread out your hands in prayer, I will turn My eyes away from you.
Even if you pray many times, I will not listen to you.
Your hands are full of blood.
passages.original: וּבְפָרִשְׂכֶ֣ם כַּפֵּיכֶ֗ם אַעְלִ֤ים עֵינַי֙ מִכֶּ֔ם גַּ֛ם כִּֽי־ תַרְבּ֥וּ תְפִלָּ֖ה אֵינֶ֣נִּי שֹׁמֵ֑עַ יְדֵיכֶ֖ם דָּמִ֥ים מָלֵֽאוּ׃

passages.text: Wash and cleanse yourselves. Remove your evil deeds from My sight. Stop doing evil!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God commands them to change.
God says, “Wash yourselves.”
God says, “Make yourselves clean.”
God says, “Remove your evil deeds from before My eyes.”
God says, “Stop doing evil.”
passages.original: רַחֲצוּ֙ הִזַּכּ֔וּ הָסִ֛ירוּ רֹ֥עַ מַעַלְלֵיכֶ֖ם מִנֶּ֣גֶד עֵינָ֑י חִדְל֖וּ הָרֵֽעַ׃

passages.text: Learn to do right; seek justice and correct the oppressor. Defend the fatherless and plead the case of the widow.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God commands them to change their ways.
Learn to do what is right.
Seek justice in all things.
Correct those who oppress others.
Defend children who have no parents.
Speak up for widows who need help.
passages.original: לִמְד֥וּ הֵיטֵ֛ב דִּרְשׁ֥וּ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט אַשְּׁר֣וּ חָמ֑וֹץ שִׁפְט֣וּ יָת֔וֹם רִ֖יבוּ אַלְמָנָֽה׃ס

passages.text: “Come now, let us reason together,” says the LORD. “Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow; though they are as red as crimson, they will become like wool.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to His people.
The LORD invites them to come and reason with Him.
The LORD says, “Come now, let us reason together.”
The LORD sees their sins.
Their sins are as red as scarlet.
Their sins are as red as crimson.
The LORD promises to cleanse them.
He will make their sins as white as snow.
He will make their sins as wool.
passages.original: לְכוּ־ נָ֛א וְנִוָּֽכְחָ֖ה יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה אִם־ יִֽהְי֨וּ חֲטָאֵיכֶ֤ם כַּשָּׁנִים֙ כַּשֶּׁ֣לֶג יַלְבִּ֔ינוּ אִם־ יַאְדִּ֥ימוּ כַתּוֹלָ֖ע כַּצֶּ֥מֶר יִהְיֽוּ׃

passages.text: If you are willing and obedient, you will eat the best of the land.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God gives a promise.
If you choose to be willing, you will receive blessing.
If you obey God, you will enjoy the best of the land.
God offers good things to those who listen and follow Him.
passages.original: אִם־ תֹּאב֖וּ וּשְׁמַעְתֶּ֑ם ט֥וּב הָאָ֖רֶץ תֹּאכֵֽלוּ׃

passages.text: But if you resist and rebel, you will be devoured by the sword.” For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
passages.sermon:
God speaks with authority.
God warns the people.
If you refuse to listen, you resist God.
If you rebel against God, you oppose Him.
You will face destruction by the sword.
God Himself has declared this.
passages.original: וְאִם־ תְּמָאֲנ֖וּ וּמְרִיתֶ֑ם חֶ֣רֶב תְּאֻכְּל֔וּ כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃ס

passages.text: See how the faithful city has become a harlot! She once was full of justice; righteousness resided within her, but now only murderers!
passages.sermon:
Jerusalem was once a faithful city.
Jerusalem was loyal to God.
Jerusalem was full of justice.
Righteousness lived in Jerusalem.
Now Jerusalem acts like a harlot.
Now murderers fill Jerusalem.
passages.original: אֵיכָה֙ הָיְתָ֣ה לְזוֹנָ֔ה קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָ֑ה מְלֵאֲתִ֣י מִשְׁפָּ֗ט צֶ֛דֶק יָלִ֥ין בָּ֖הּ וְעַתָּ֥ה מְרַצְּחִֽים׃

passages.text: Your silver has become dross; your fine wine is diluted with water.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem was once faithful.
Now Jerusalem has changed.
Your silver is no longer pure.
Your silver has become dross.
Your wine is no longer strong.
Your wine is mixed with water.
passages.original: כַּסְפֵּ֖ךְ הָיָ֣ה לְסִיגִ֑ים סָבְאֵ֖ךְ מָה֥וּל בַּמָּֽיִם׃

passages.text: Your rulers are rebels, friends of thieves. They all love bribes and chasing after rewards. They do not defend the fatherless, and the plea of the widow never comes before them.
passages.sermon:
The rulers in Jerusalem are rebels.
They are friends of thieves.
They all love bribes.
They all chase after rewards.
They do not defend the fatherless.
The plea of the widow never comes before them.
passages.original: שָׂרַ֣יִךְ סוֹרְרִ֗ים וְחַבְרֵי֙ גַּנָּבִ֔ים כֻּלּוֹ֙ אֹהֵ֣ב שֹׁ֔חַד וְרֹדֵ֖ף שַׁלְמֹנִ֑ים יָתוֹם֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁפֹּ֔טוּ וְרִ֥יב אַלְמָנָ֖ה לֹֽא־ יָב֥וֹא אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃פ

passages.text: Therefore the Lord GOD of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, declares: “Ah, I will be relieved of My foes and avenge Myself on My enemies.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is God of Hosts.
He is the Mighty One of Israel.
The Lord speaks.
He says, “I will act against My foes.
I will find relief from those who oppose Me.
I will take vengeance on My enemies.”
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן נְאֻ֤ם הָֽאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֲבִ֖יר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ה֚וֹי אֶנָּחֵ֣ם מִצָּרַ֔י וְאִנָּקְמָ֖ה מֵאוֹיְבָֽי׃

passages.text: I will turn My hand against you; I will thoroughly purge your dross; I will remove all your impurities.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is the Mighty One of Israel.
The Lord speaks to His people.
The Lord says, “I will turn My hand against you.
I will burn away your dross like a refiner.
I will remove all your impurities.”
passages.original: וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה יָדִי֙ עָלַ֔יִךְ וְאֶצְרֹ֥ף כַּבֹּ֖ר סִיגָ֑יִךְ וְאָסִ֖ירָה כָּל־ בְּדִילָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: I will restore your judges as at first, and your counselors as at the beginning. After that you will be called the City of Righteousness, the Faithful City.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord is the Mighty One of Israel.
The Lord speaks to His people.
The Lord says, "I will restore your judges."
Your judges will be as they were at first.
I will restore your counselors.
Your counselors will be as they were in the beginning.
After this, people will call you the City of Righteousness.
People will call you the Faithful City.
passages.original: וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה שֹׁפְטַ֙יִךְ֙ כְּבָרִ֣אשֹׁנָ֔ה וְיֹעֲצַ֖יִךְ כְּבַתְּחִלָּ֑ה אַחֲרֵי־ כֵ֗ן יִקָּ֤רֵא לָךְ֙ עִ֣יר הַצֶּ֔דֶק קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָֽה׃

passages.text: Zion will be redeemed with justice, her repentant ones with righteousness.
passages.sermon:
Zion is a city.
God will redeem Zion.
God will use justice to redeem Zion.
God will also redeem the people who return to Him.
God will use righteousness to redeem those people.
passages.original: צִיּ֖וֹן בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט תִּפָּדֶ֑ה וְשָׁבֶ֖יהָ בִּצְדָקָֽה׃

passages.text: But rebels and sinners will together be shattered, and those who forsake the LORD will perish.
passages.sermon:
Rebels will be shattered.
Sinners will be shattered.
They will be shattered together.
People who forsake the LORD will perish.
passages.original: וְשֶׁ֧בֶר פֹּשְׁעִ֛ים וְחַטָּאִ֖ים יַחְדָּ֑ו וְעֹזְבֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה יִכְלֽוּ׃

passages.text: Surely you will be ashamed of the sacred oaks in which you have delighted; you will be embarrassed by the gardens that you have chosen.
passages.sermon:
God spoke through Isaiah to the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
God warned those who delighted in sacred oaks.
You will feel shame because you desired these oaks.
You chose certain gardens for yourselves.
You will feel embarrassment because of these gardens.
passages.original: כִּ֣י יֵבֹ֔שׁוּ מֵאֵילִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר חֲמַדְתֶּ֑ם וְתַ֨חְפְּר֔וּ מֵהַגַּנּ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּחַרְתֶּֽם׃

passages.text: For you will become like an oak whose leaves are withered, like a garden without water.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to those who turn away from Him.
You will become weak and lifeless.
You will be like an oak tree with dry, withered leaves.
You will be like a garden that has no water.
You will have no strength or life in you.
passages.original: כִּ֣י תִֽהְי֔וּ כְּאֵלָ֖ה נֹבֶ֣לֶת עָלֶ֑הָ וּֽכְגַנָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ מַ֖יִם אֵ֥ין לָֽהּ׃

passages.text: The strong man will become tinder and his work will be a spark; both will burn together, with no one to quench the flames.
passages.sermon:
Isaiah spoke a message from God about Judah and Jerusalem.
A strong man will become like dry tinder.
His work will become like a spark.
Both the man and his work will burn together.
No one will put out the fire.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֤ה הֶחָסֹן֙ לִנְעֹ֔רֶת וּפֹעֲל֖וֹ לְנִיצ֑וֹץ וּבָעֲר֧וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֛ם יַחְדָּ֖ו וְאֵ֥ין מְכַבֶּֽה׃ס
